Closest precedents concern adaptive interest fusion, rather than the exact SASRec-plus-coherence-gated-mean residual. [CLSR (WWW 2022)](https://fi.ee.tsinghua.edu.cn/~gaochen/papers/WWW2022-CLSR.pdf) uses separate long/short-term encoders, mean-pooled history/recent-history proxies for contrastive supervision, and adaptive attention fusion. [TLSRec (CIKM 2022)](https://yneversky.github.io/Papers/cikm22.pdf) combines hierarchical self-attention, short-term session average pooling, and a dimension-wise time-lag gate; its ablations remove attention before pooling or replace gated fusion with averaging. [PAN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.15346) learns contextual, time-aware short-term interests and gates their fusion with long-term interests. These establish relevant fusion baselines, but do not establish that cosine coherence improves a SASRec residual.

Key mathematical confound: for n unit-normalized item embeddings, mean m, and average pairwise cosine c over distinct pairs, ||m||² = [1+(n−1)c]/n. Thus pairwise cosine coherence and normalized-pooling magnitude encode exactly the same information conditional on n. A gate based on that coherence cannot add independent information beyond magnitude and sequence length, although its parameterization can change optimization. Raw-embedding pooling also incorporates varying item norms; last-item-to-pool cosine is a different statistic.

Recommended controlled ablations: SASRec alone; h+m; h+αm with validation-tuned constant α; learned global α; magnitude-and-length gate; cosine-coherence gate; learned content gate using h and m; and shuffled gates preserving the gate distribution. Repeat with normalized pooling vectors to control residual amplitude, and compare raw versus unit-normalized item embeddings. Match windows, loss, training budget, and tuning allowance. These are proposed controls, not reported results: only improvement over magnitude/length and tuned scaling supports expanding the gate architecture.
